title: False 911 Recovery Report — Social Media Pressure

fields.avatarBrief: person with raised eyebrow, neutral expression, sitting at a desk with a laptop and phone
fields.text: Official 911 update says they’re back online — but calls are still going to the wrong firehouse. A caller in Marlow said they got patched to Engine 7, not Engine 1. Is 911 really fixed? #RookCounty #911StillDown
fields.attachedImageBrief: phone photo of a cracked smartphone screen showing a fake 911 status page with 'System Restored' and a map pointing to a wrong firehouse
fields.attachedImageAlt: Cracked phone screen with a fake 911 system status page showing incorrect firehouse routing

instructorNote: This inject applies pressure on the PIO to verify system integrity and correct misinformation quickly. Watch for delays in WEA or social media correction, and whether the EOC hotline is activated.

citations.documentTitle: Rook County Emergency Communications District — ECC Operations and Continuity Plan
citations.quote: The PIO publishes alternate 10-digit emergency numbers only on the Director's decision (OPS-DR-4) and only numbers in Annex A. The message always says "If you can reach 911, keep calling 911." Channel

citations.documentTitle: Rook County Emergency Communications District — Systems, Positions and Radio Description
citations.quote: | PSAP | Agreement | Ring-down | |---|---|---| | Tamarack County Communications | Mutual call-taking (MCTA-2025); receives rerouted 911 | Yes | | Juniper County 911 | Mutual aid radio patch on 8TAC91

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. A close-up phone snapshot taken from above, showing a cracked smartphone screen displaying a fake 911 system status page. The screen is dimly lit, glowing green and red, with a map overlay pointing to a wrong firehouse in Marlow. The device lies on a desk in a cluttered home office, partially obscured by a coffee mug and a notebook. A hand with a silver ring is visible at the edge, gripping the phone. The background is out of focus, showing a wall with framed photos and a calendar. The camera angle is slightly tilted, lens flared from ambient light. Mood: tense, urgent, digital misinformation. Setting: a resident on a front porch calling 911 on a mobile phone, a patrol car pulling up to the curb with its light bar on, neighbors watching from the sidewalk, dusk
